solution:
The region is bounded by the line \(y = 2x\), the X-axis, and the ordinates \(x = 0\) and \(x = 5\). Since \(y \ge 0\) on \([0, 5]\), the area is
\(A = \int_0^5 y\,dx = \int_0^5 2x\,dx\)
\(A = 2\left[\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^5 = \left[x^2\right]_0^5\)
\(A = 5^2 - 0 = 25\)
\(A = 25\) sq. units.

The region is bounded by the line \(x = 2y\), the Y-axis, and \(y = 0,\ y = 4\). Integrating with respect to \(y\),
\(A = \int_0^4 x\,dy = \int_0^4 2y\,dy\)
\(A = 2\left[\dfrac{y^2}{2}\right]_0^4 = \left[y^2\right]_0^4\)
\(A = 4^2 - 0 = 16\)
\(A = 16\) sq. units.

The region is the rectangle bounded by \(x = 0,\ x = 5,\ y = 0,\ y = 4\). Here the top boundary is the line \(y = 4\), so
\(A = \int_0^5 y\,dx = \int_0^5 4\,dx\)
\(A = 4\left[x\right]_0^5 = 4(5 - 0)\)
\(A = 20\)
\(A = 20\) sq. units.

The region is bounded by \(y = \sin x\), the X-axis, and \(x = 0,\ x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\). Since \(\sin x \ge 0\) on \(\left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]\),
\(A = \int_0^{\pi/2} y\,dx = \int_0^{\pi/2} \sin x\,dx\)
\(A = \left[-\cos x\right]_0^{\pi/2}\)
\(A = -\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2} + \cos 0 = -0 + 1\)
\(A = 1\) sq. unit.

The curve \(xy = 2\) gives \(y = \dfrac{2}{x}\), and the region is bounded by the X-axis with \(x = 1,\ x = 4\). Since \(y > 0\) here,
\(A = \int_1^4 y\,dx = \int_1^4 \dfrac{2}{x}\,dx\)
\(A = 2\left[\log x\right]_1^4 = 2\left(\log 4 - \log 1\right)\)
\(A = 2\log 4 = 4\log 2\)
\(A = 4\log 2\) sq. units.

The parabola \(y^2 = x\) in the first quadrant gives \(y = \sqrt{x}\); the region is bounded by the X-axis and \(x = 0,\ x = 4\).
\(A = \int_0^4 y\,dx = \int_0^4 \sqrt{x}\,dx = \int_0^4 x^{1/2}\,dx\)
\(A = \left[\dfrac{x^{3/2}}{3/2}\right]_0^4 = \dfrac{2}{3}\left[x^{3/2}\right]_0^4\)
\(A = \dfrac{2}{3}\left(4^{3/2} - 0\right) = \dfrac{2}{3}(8)\)
\(A = \dfrac{16}{3}\) sq. units.

The parabola \(y^2 = 16x\) in the first quadrant gives \(y = 4\sqrt{x}\); the region is bounded by the X-axis and \(x = 0,\ x = 4\).
\(A = \int_0^4 y\,dx = \int_0^4 4\sqrt{x}\,dx = 4\int_0^4 x^{1/2}\,dx\)
\(A = 4 \cdot \dfrac{2}{3}\left[x^{3/2}\right]_0^4 = \dfrac{8}{3}\left(4^{3/2} - 0\right)\)
\(A = \dfrac{8}{3}(8) = \dfrac{64}{3}\)
\(A = \dfrac{64}{3}\) sq. units.

For the parabola \(y^2 = 16x\), comparing with \(y^2 = 4ax\) gives \(4a = 16\), so \(a = 4\). Its latus rectum is the line \(x = a = 4\). In the first quadrant \(y = 4\sqrt{x}\), and the region enclosed by the parabola and its latus rectum is symmetric about the X-axis, so
\(A = 2\int_0^4 y\,dx = 2\int_0^4 4\sqrt{x}\,dx = 8\int_0^4 x^{1/2}\,dx\)
\(A = 8 \cdot \dfrac{2}{3}\left[x^{3/2}\right]_0^4 = \dfrac{16}{3}\left(4^{3/2}\right)\)
\(A = \dfrac{16}{3}(8) = \dfrac{128}{3}\)
\(A = \dfrac{128}{3}\) sq. units.

The parabola \(y = 4 - x^2\) meets the X-axis where \(y = 0\), i.e. \(4 - x^2 = 0\), giving \(x = -2\) and \(x = 2\). The curve lies above the X-axis on \([-2, 2]\), and by symmetry about the Y-axis,
\(A = \int_{-2}^{2} (4 - x^2)\,dx = 2\int_0^2 (4 - x^2)\,dx\)
\(A = 2\left[4x - \dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^2 = 2\left(8 - \dfrac{8}{3}\right)\)
\(A = 2 \cdot \dfrac{16}{3} = \dfrac{32}{3}\)
\(A = \dfrac{32}{3}\) sq. units.

Curves: parabola \(y^2 = 2x\) and line \(y = 2x\). For intersection, substitute \(2x = y^2\) into \(y = 2x\): \(y = y^2 \Rightarrow y(y - 1) = 0\), so \(y = 0\) or \(y = 1\). The points are \((0, 0)\) and \(\left(\dfrac{1}{2}, 1\right)\).
Integrating with respect to \(y\): rightmost boundary is the line \(x = \dfrac{y}{2}\), leftmost is the parabola \(x = \dfrac{y^2}{2}\).
\(A = \int_0^1 \left(\dfrac{y}{2} - \dfrac{y^2}{2}\right) dy = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{y^2}{2} - \dfrac{y^3}{3}\right]_0^1\)
\(A = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{6}\)
\(A = \dfrac{1}{12}\) sq. units.

Curves: parabola \(y^2 = 4x\) and line \(y = x\). For intersection, put \(x = y\) into \(y^2 = 4x\): \(y^2 = 4y \Rightarrow y(y - 4) = 0\), so \(y = 0\) or \(y = 4\). The points are \((0, 0)\) and \((4, 4)\).
Integrating with respect to \(y\): rightmost boundary is the line \(x = y\), leftmost is the parabola \(x = \dfrac{y^2}{4}\).
\(A = \int_0^4 \left(y - \dfrac{y^2}{4}\right) dy = \left[\dfrac{y^2}{2} - \dfrac{y^3}{12}\right]_0^4\)
\(A = \dfrac{16}{2} - \dfrac{64}{12} = 8 - \dfrac{16}{3}\)
\(A = \dfrac{24 - 16}{3} = \dfrac{8}{3}\)
\(A = \dfrac{8}{3}\) sq. units.

Curves: parabola \(y = x^2\) and line \(y = 4x\). For intersection, \(x^2 = 4x \Rightarrow x(x - 4) = 0\), so \(x = 0\) or \(x = 4\). The points are \((0, 0)\) and \((4, 16)\). On \([0, 4]\) the line \(y = 4x\) lies above the parabola \(y = x^2\).
\(A = \int_0^4 (4x - x^2)\,dx = \left[2x^2 - \dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^4\)
\(A = 2(16) - \dfrac{64}{3} = 32 - \dfrac{64}{3}\)
\(A = \dfrac{96 - 64}{3} = \dfrac{32}{3}\)
\(A = \dfrac{32}{3}\) sq. units.

Curves: parabola \(y^2 = 4ax\) and line \(y = x\). For intersection, put \(y = x\): \(x^2 = 4ax \Rightarrow x(x - 4a) = 0\), so \(x = 0\) or \(x = 4a\). The points are \((0, 0)\) and \((4a, 4a)\). On \([0, 4a]\) the parabola \(y = 2\sqrt{a}\,\sqrt{x}\) lies above the line \(y = x\).
\(A = \int_0^{4a} \left(2\sqrt{a}\,\sqrt{x} - x\right) dx\)
\(A = 2\sqrt{a}\cdot\dfrac{2}{3}\left[x^{3/2}\right]_0^{4a} - \left[\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^{4a}\)
\(A = \dfrac{4\sqrt{a}}{3}(4a)^{3/2} - \dfrac{(4a)^2}{2} = \dfrac{4\sqrt{a}}{3}\left(8a\sqrt{a}\right) - \dfrac{16a^2}{2}\)
\(A = \dfrac{32a^2}{3} - 8a^2 = \dfrac{32a^2 - 24a^2}{3}\)
\(A = \dfrac{8a^2}{3}\) sq. units.

Curves: parabola \(y = x^2 + 3\) and line \(y = x + 3\). For intersection, \(x^2 + 3 = x + 3 \Rightarrow x^2 - x = 0 \Rightarrow x(x - 1) = 0\), so \(x = 0\) or \(x = 1\). The points are \((0, 3)\) and \((1, 4)\). On \([0, 1]\) the line \(y = x + 3\) lies above the parabola \(y = x^2 + 3\).
\(A = \int_0^1 \left[(x + 3) - (x^2 + 3)\right] dx = \int_0^1 (x - x^2)\,dx\)
\(A = \left[\dfrac{x^2}{2} - \dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^1 = \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{3}\)
\(A = \dfrac{3 - 2}{6} = \dfrac{1}{6}\)
\(A = \dfrac{1}{6}\) sq. units.
